messages:
jane_cust: Hey team — trying to pay invoice INV-3142 with company corporate card and it keeps declining. Card issuer says 'merchant category not allowed'. can you confirm what's blocked?

emma_support: sorry about that — can you DM the last 4 of the card and the exact timestamp (UTC) when you tried? also did you see a decline code or message on the checkout page?

jane_cust: sent DM with last4 4321 and timestamp 2026-03-15T16:42:10Z. On-screen it just said 'Payment declined'. No extra info.

oleg_billing: I pulled the gateway events for INV-3142. Payments processor (Stripe) shows a decline with metadata indicating MCC block. excerpt: ```
{
  event: "payment_intent.payment_failed",
  pi: "pi_3JxXxx",
  decline_code: "generic_decline",
  outcome: {reason: "mcc_blocked", seller_message: "Do not honor"},
  gateway_metadata: {mcc: "5812", mcc_description: "Eating places, restaurants"}
}
```

li_eng: quick note: MCC 5812 is often blocked by corp cards for restaurants. The gateway shows `mcc: 5812` in metadata and `reason: mcc_blocked`. That means the customer's card admin set a merchant category restriction, not an issue in our tokenization or PCI.

matt_finance: If their policy forbids restaurants we can't change the card controls. Options: 1) vendor/merchant whitelist from their card admin, 2) process via PO/wire/ACH, or 3) have them pay with a different card that allows MCC 5812.

jane_cust: company policy forbids wires for < $10k and they only let ops do whitelists. Invoice is $2,860 so wiring will be denied. Is there any way to mark this invoice as "software" or change MCC on our side?

emma_support: we cannot change how the merchant category is reported — it's set by the merchant bank at transaction time. We could ask the merchant to be reclassified, but that requires merchant/processor coordination and is slow. I'll escalate to payments team to confirm if any workaround exists for cases like this.

payments-bot: New escalation ticket created: PAY-2026-117. Assigned to payments escalation queue.

li_eng: For the record, I've validated the flow: we sent the correct MCC from our side (5812). Repro steps: 1) Invoices > click Pay > enter card > submit 2) PaymentIntent created, card auth attempted 3) Payment failed with `outcome.reason = mcc_blocked` and Stripe decline_code `generic_decline`. So it's upstream at the card network or issuer.

oleg_billing: jane, two practical suggestions while escalation runs: - Ask your card admin to temporarily whitelist vendor MCC 5812 for a single merchant or transaction - Or add a different corporate card that allows restaurant MCCs to your billing profile

jane_cust: I'll contact our finance admin now. If they need a formal request from Redwood, can you provide a short note explaining the transaction (merchant name, MCC, mid)?

emma_support: yes — I can draft. details: merchant: Redwood Inference Billing, MID: 6789012, MCC: 5812, invoice: INV-3142, amount: $2,860, attempted at 2026-03-15T16:42:10Z. I'll post the note in the escalation ticket and share it with you.

matt_finance: Also adding fallback: if they cannot whitelist, we can offer a 7-day net invoice via ACH as a one-off for this customer while they sort their card controls. I'll coordinate with legal on T&Cs.

jane_cust: appreciated. please include a line that they attempted to pay by card before asking whitelist. that usually helps admin.

emma_support: done — I've updated PAY-2026-117 with the copy and attached the gateway logs. Also added contact point for the customer admin (jane_cust@acme.co) so payments team can reach out if needed.

oleg_billing: marking this thread for follow-up. I'll update INV-3142 notes with the escalation id and fallback ACH option. :eyes:

jane_cust: thanks all :thumbsup:
